 Annual Floods Force Homemaker To Keep Furniture Upstairs Year-Round
 09/11/2026 04:47 PM 
 KUALA BERANG, Nov 9 (Bernama) -- Having experienced floods almost every Northeast Monsoon season, a homemaker in Kampung Paya Besar here keeps almost all her belongings and furniture on the upper floor of her house throughout the year.
 Musfirah Sidik, 37, said only a few items, including wooden chairs for guests and a cooking stove, were kept downstairs for use during the dry season, while other belongings such as beds and wardrobes remained upstairs.
 "I have lived in this house since marrying my husband, Husni Nadawi Mohd Nawi, 40, in 2013. We experience floods every year, and I grew tired of having to move our belongings repeatedly. So my husband and I decided to keep everything upstairs permanently.
 "Moreover, I was diagnosed with thyroid cancer two years ago and am no longer physically strong enough to move furniture and clean the house every time it floods," she told Bernama at her home in Kampung Paya Besar here today.
 The mother of six children, aged between two and 11, said her house was flooded every rainy season, with water levels reaching as high as three metres due to its location about one kilometre from Sungai Berang.
 However, she said her family rarely moved to a temporary relief centre (PPS) as the upper floor of their house was equipped with basic necessities, including a kitchen and toilet, allowing them to remain there throughout the flood season.
 "However, if the flooding becomes too severe, we will move to a PPS on the advice of security personnel, as we did in 2024 when the water rose rapidly and we became concerned for our safety," she said.
 Meanwhile, Sasuhaida Sulaiman, 42, from Kampung Laut near Kuala Terengganu, said her experience of dealing with annual floods had prompted her and her husband to prepare bags containing clothes and important documents in advance to facilitate evacuation if water levels rose suddenly.
 The mother of three children, aged between 12 and 19, said her family had to move to a PPS every year because their house was in a low-lying area near a swamp.
 "As our house is flooded every year, we place wooden blocks under electrical appliances such as the washing machine and refrigerator to raise them above floor level in preparation for floods.
 "But the monsoon season has arrived slightly later this year. It started raining last night, but so far the water is only outside the house and has not entered. The rain has also not been continuous, allowing the water to recede," she said.
 Another resident, Mohd Norzilan Ismail, 50, of Taman Desa Tanjung Damai near Gong Badak in Kuala Nerus, said he had also prepared important documents and rented a four-wheel-drive vehicle to move electrical appliances and furniture to safety in anticipation of flooding.
 "I previously installed a wooden barrier in front of my house to prevent water from entering, but it was ineffective when heavy rain continued for days and water levels rose.
 "Since moving here in 2012, my house has been flooded almost every year. Sometimes the water only reaches ankle or knee level, but the worst flooding was in 2014, when the house was submerged.
 "To prevent more belongings from being damaged, I have arranged with a friend to use a four-wheel-drive vehicle to move them. For now, the rain appears manageable. If the rain continues for another 24 hours, I will move my belongings to a safe place," he said.
 Yesterday, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) issued a continuous rain warning for several areas in Kelantan, Pahang and Sabah, as well as the whole of Terengganu, until Wednesday.
